text: Functools is a treasure chest of tools that supercharge your functions.
The lru_cache decorator remembers past results, so repeated calls return instantly instead of recomputing.
Slap it on a recursive fibonacci, and computing the fiftieth number becomes immediate.
[chuckle] Without caching, that same call would trigger billions of redundant computations.
[sniff] partial creates a new function by pre-filling some of another function's arguments.
Here we lock exp to two, turning the general power function into a dedicated square function.
[sigh] reduce folds an entire sequence down to a single value, applying a function pairwise.
Multiplying the list one, two, three, four step by step gives twenty-four, the product of them all.
[groan] Caching, partials, and reduce are the kind of tools that make advanced Python both faster and more elegant.
Up next, the collections module. Save this one for when you need it.
